subject: DI01000021

intro_text.en: Unit 4 of Mathematics-I: the straight line - its slope and the four standard forms (slope-intercept, point-slope, two-point and intercept), the general form ax + by + c = 0, the conditions for two lines to be parallel or perpendicular and the angle between them; the distance of a point from a line and the distance between two parallel lines; then the circle - centre-radius form, general form, centre and radius from the coefficients, the tangent and normal at a point, and the length of a tangent drawn from an external point, following syllabus items 4.1 to 4.7. Twenty-six fully solved numericals.

h.en: 1.1 Slope and the two-point form

body.en:
Definition

The slope of a line is m = tan θ, where θ is the angle it makes with the positive x-axis. Between two points it is m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) - rise over run.

Two-point form

The line through (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is (y − y₁)(x₂ − x₁) = (y₂ − y₁)(x − x₁), which is just the slope formula written as an equation.

Worked example

Through (1, 2) and (3, 8): m = 6/2 = 3, so y − 2 = 3(x − 1), that is 3x − y − 1 = 0. Check the second point: 9 − 8 − 1 = 0 ✓.

Common mistake / conditions

A vertical line has no finite slope (x₂ = x₁) and its equation is x = a. Never write y = mx + c for a vertical line - that form cannot represent it.

h.en: 1.2 Slope-point and intercept forms

body.en:
The four forms

FormEquationUse it when you know
Slope-intercepty = mx + cslope and y-intercept
Point-slopey − y₁ = m(x − x₁)one point and the slope
Two-point(y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁)two points
Interceptx/a + y/b = 1the intercepts a on x and b on y

Worked examples

Through (−2, 3) with m = 1/2: y − 3 = ½(x + 2) → 2y − 6 = x + 2 → x − 2y + 8 = 0.

Intercepts 3 and −4: x/3 + y/(−4) = 1 → 4x − 3y = 12.

Conditions

The intercept form needs both intercepts non-zero. A line through the origin has no intercept form; use y = mx.

h.en: 1.3 The general form and converting between forms

body.en:
Definition

Every line can be written ax + by + c = 0 with a and b not both zero. From it, slope = −a/b and intercepts are −c/a (x) and −c/b (y).

Worked example

3x + 4y − 12 = 0 → y = −(3/4)x + 3 (slope −3/4, y-intercept 3) and x/4 + y/3 = 1 (intercepts 4 and 3). Both come from the same equation - choose the form the question asks for.

Common mistake / conditions

The slope is −a/b, not a/b. A quick check: for 3x + 4y = 12 the line falls as x grows, so the slope must be negative ✓.

h.en: 2.1 The two slope conditions

body.en:
Conditions

Parallel: m₁ = m₂. Perpendicular: m₁m₂ = −1, that is m₂ = −1/m₁.

In general form

For a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0: parallel when a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂, perpendicular when a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 0.

Worked example

3x + 4y = 7 and 6x + 8y = 15 are parallel (coefficient ratios 1/2 and 1/2, constants different). 3x + 4y = 7 and 4x − 3y = 2 are perpendicular because 3(4) + 4(−3) = 0.

Why m₁m₂ = −1

Rotating a line by 90° turns its rise into a run: a slope of p/q becomes −q/p. Their product is −pq/qp = −1. That is the whole proof, and it explains the sign change.

h.en: 2.2 Lines parallel or perpendicular to a given line

body.en:
The two-line trick

To draw a line parallel to ax + by + c = 0 through a point, keep a and b and change only c. To draw a perpendicular, swap a and b and change the sign of one of them.

Worked examples

Parallel to 3x − 4y + 5 = 0 through (2, −3): the family is 3x − 4y + k = 0. Substituting gives 6 + 12 + k = 0, so k = −18 and the line is 3x − 4y − 18 = 0.

Perpendicular to 2x + 3y = 6 through (1, 2): the family is 3x − 2y + k = 0, and 3 − 4 + k = 0 gives k = 1, so 3x − 2y + 1 = 0.

Common mistake / conditions

Substituting the point into the family, not into the original line, is what finds k. Writing the original constant again gives a parallel line that misses the point.

title.en: 3. Angle between Two Lines and Distances

h.en: 3.1 The angle formula

body.en:
Formula

tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)|, the acute angle between two lines of slopes m₁ and m₂.

Procedure

  1. Write both lines in slope form and read m₁, m₂.
  2. Substitute into the formula; the modulus makes θ acute.
  3. If the question wants the obtuse angle, subtract from 180°.

Worked example

y = 2x + 1 and y = −x + 3: tan θ = |(2 + 1)/(1 − 2)| = 3, so θ = tan⁻¹3 ≈ 71.57°.

Special cases

If 1 + m₁m₂ = 0 the denominator vanishes and θ = 90° - the perpendicular condition. If m₁ = m₂ the numerator vanishes and θ = 0°: the lines are parallel.

h.en: 3.2 Distance from a point to a line, and between parallel lines

body.en:
Formulae

Point to line: d = |ax₁ + by₁ + c| / √(a² + b²) for the point (x₁, y₁) and the line ax + by + c = 0.

Between parallel lines ax + by + c₁ = 0 and ax + by + c₂ = 0: d = |c₁ − c₂| / √(a² + b²).

Worked examples

(2, 3) to 3x + 4y − 5 = 0: |6 + 12 − 5|/√25 = 13/5 = 2.6 units. The lines 3x + 4y = 5 and 3x + 4y = 15 are |5 − 15|/5 = 2 units apart.

Conditions

Both lines must be in the same form before comparing constants. The distance is never negative - the modulus is part of the formula.

h.en: 4.1 Centre-radius form

body.en:
Definition

A circle is the set of points at a fixed distance r from a fixed point (h, k). Its equation is

(x − h)² + (y − k)² = r².

From the definition

For any point P(x, y) on the circle, the distance CP equals r. Squaring the distance formula √((x − h)² + (y − k)²) = r gives the equation - no memorising needed.

Worked example

Centre (2, −3), radius 5: (x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 25, which expands to x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0.

Conditions

Watch the signs: centre (2, −3) gives (y + 3)², not (y − 3)². The right side is r², so a radius of 5 puts 25 there.

h.en: 4.2 The general equation and how to read it

body.en:
Definition

The general circle is x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0, with centre (−g, −f) and radius √(g² + f² − c).

Where it comes from

Expand (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²: x² + y² − 2hx − 2ky + h² + k² − r² = 0. Comparing with the general form gives g = −h, f = −k and c = h² + k² − r², hence the radius formula.

Worked example

x² + y² − 6x + 8y − 11 = 0: g = −3, f = 4, c = −11, so centre (3, −4) and radius √(9 + 16 + 11) = 6.

Conditions

The coefficients of x² and y² must both be 1 before reading g and f; divide through if they are not. If g² + f² − c < 0 the equation has no real circle.

h.en: 4.3 Circle from a diameter or three conditions

body.en:
Diameter form

If (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) are the ends of a diameter, the circle is (x − x₁)(x − x₂) + (y − y₁)(y − y₂) = 0, because the angle in a semicircle is 90°.

Worked example

Diameter ends (1, 2) and (5, 8): centre (3, 5) and radius ½√(16 + 36) = √13, so (x − 3)² + (y − 5)² = 13. The diameter form gives the same circle.

Three points

A circle through three points needs all three in the general equation, which gives three linear equations in g, f, c. Through the origin c = 0 immediately, which is why exam questions like to pass circles through (0, 0).

title.en: 5. Tangent and Normal to a Circle

h.en: 5.1 Tangent at a point on the circle

body.en:
Definition

A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point. At the point of contact it is perpendicular to the radius, so its slope is the negative reciprocal of the radius slope.

Formula for x² + y² = a²

The tangent at (x₁, y₁) on the circle is xx₁ + yy₁ = a² - replace x² by xx₁ and y² by yy₁. For a general circle, use the point-slope form with the perpendicular slope.

Worked example

At (3, 4) on x² + y² = 25: the tangent is 3x + 4y = 25. Its slope is −3/4 while the radius slope is 4/3, and (4/3)(−3/4) = −1 ✓.

Common mistake / conditions

The formula needs the point to lie on the circle: check 3² + 4² = 25 first. Using an external point with this formula gives the chord of contact, not the tangent.

h.en: 5.2 Tangents of a given slope, and the normal

body.en:
Tangent with slope m

For x² + y² = a² the tangents of slope m are y = mx ± a√(1 + m²). The ± gives two parallel tangents, one on each side.

Worked example

Slope 3/4 to x² + y² = 25: c = ±5√(1 + 9/16) = ±25/4, so the tangents are y = (3/4)x ± 25/4, that is 3x − 4y ± 25 = 0.

Normal

The normal at a point passes through the centre, so for x² + y² = a² it is simply the line joining the centre to that point: through (3, 4) it is y = (4/3)x, or 4x − 3y = 0.

Length of a tangent from an external point

From P(x₁, y₁) to x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 the length is √(x₁² + y₁² + 2gx₁ + 2fy₁ + c). From (5, 1) to x² + y² = 25 it is √(26 − 25) = 1.

h.en: 5.3 Tangency condition: when a line just touches

body.en:
The test

A line touches a circle when the perpendicular distance from the centre equals the radius. That single condition replaces every "show that the line is a tangent" proof.

Worked example

Is y = 2x + c tangent to x² + y² = 25? The distance from (0, 0) to 2x − y + c = 0 is |c|/√5, so tangency requires |c|/√5 = 5, giving c = ±5√5.

Three cases

Distance from centreLine meets the circleName
d < rat two pointssecant
d = rat exactly one pointtangent
d > rnot at allexternal line

Why this is the safest method

Solving the line and circle simultaneously gives a quadratic; the discriminant then decides the case. Both routes are correct, but the distance test is shorter and has fewer sign traps.

h.en: Practice 1. Find the slope and equation of the line through (0, 5) and (3, 11).

body.en:
Working

  1. m = (11 − 5)/(3 − 0) = 2
  2. y − 5 = 2(x − 0)
  3. y = 2x + 5

Answer

Slope 2, equation 2x − y + 5 = 0. Check both points: 0 − 5 + 5 = 0 ✓ and 6 − 11 + 5 = 0 ✓.

h.en: Practice 2. Find the equation of the line with slope −3 passing through (2, 4).

body.en:
Working

  1. Start from y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) with m = −3 and (x₁, y₁) = (2, 4)
  2. y − 4 = −3(x − 2)
  3. y − 4 = −3x + 6
  4. y = −3x + 10, that is 3x + y − 10 = 0

Answer

3x + y − 10 = 0. Check: 6 + 4 − 10 = 0 ✓, the y-intercept is 10 ✓, and the slope −a/b = −3 ✓. As a final form, a straight-line answer is safest with integer coefficients and a positive x-term.

h.en: Practice 3. Find the equation of the line whose intercepts are −2 on x and 5 on y.

body.en:
Working

  1. x/(−2) + y/5 = 1
  2. Multiply by 10: −5x + 2y = 10
  3. 5x − 2y + 10 = 0

Answer

5x − 2y + 10 = 0. Check the intercepts: at y = 0, x = −2 ✓; at x = 0, y = 5 ✓.

h.en: Practice 4. Show that the lines 5x − 2y + 3 = 0 and 10x − 4y − 7 = 0 are parallel.

body.en:
Working

  1. For ax + by + c = 0 the slope is −a/b
  2. First line: −5/(−2) = 5/2
  3. Second line: −10/(−4) = 5/2
  4. Ratio test: 5/10 = (−2)/(−4) = 1/2, but 3/(−7) ≠ 1/2

Answer

Parallel and distinct. Both have slope 5/2, and because the constant ratio differs the two lines never meet. Had all three ratios matched, they would be the same line rather than two parallel ones.

h.en: Practice 5. Find the equation of the line through (3, −1) perpendicular to 4x − 3y + 7 = 0.

body.en:
Working

  1. Perpendicular family: 3x + 4y + k = 0
  2. 3(3) + 4(−1) + k = 0
  3. k = −5
  4. 3x + 4y − 5 = 0

Check

a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 4(3) + (−3)(4) = 0 ✓ and the point satisfies the new line ✓.

h.en: Practice 6. Find the acute angle between 2x − y + 3 = 0 and x + 3y − 2 = 0.

body.en:
Working

  1. m₁ = 2 and m₂ = −1/3
  2. tan θ = |(2 + 1/3)/(1 − 2/3)| = |(7/3)/(1/3)| = 7
  3. θ = 81.87°

Answer

θ ≈ 81.9°. The coefficient test gives 2(1) + (−1)(3) = −1, close to zero, so the lines are nearly perpendicular ✓.

h.en: Practice 7. Find the distance between the parallel lines 4x + 3y − 9 = 0 and 4x + 3y + 6 = 0.

body.en:
Working

  1. |−9 − 6| = 15
  2. √(16 + 9) = 5
  3. d = 15/5 = 3

Answer

3 units. Check with a point: (0, 3) lies on the first line and its distance from the second is |0 + 9 + 6|/5 = 3 ✓.

h.en: Practice 8. Find the centre and radius of x² + y² + 4x − 6y − 12 = 0.

body.en:
Working

  1. 2g = 4 → g = 2; 2f = −6 → f = −3; c = −12
  2. Centre (−2, 3)
  3. r = √(4 + 9 + 12) = √25 = 5

Answer

Centre (−2, 3), radius 5. Check by completing the square: (x + 2)² + (y − 3)² = 25 ✓.

h.en: Practice 9. Find the equation of the circle with centre (−1, 2) passing through (3, 5).

body.en:
Working

  1. r = √((3 + 1)² + (5 − 2)²) = √(16 + 9) = 5
  2. (x + 1)² + (y − 2)² = 25
  3. x² + y² + 2x − 4y − 20 = 0

Check

The point (3, 5) satisfies 16 + 9 = 25 ✓. The expanded form has centre (−1, 2) again ✓.

h.en: Practice 10. Find the tangent to x² + y² = 169 at (5, 12).

body.en:
Working

The point is on the circle because 25 + 144 = 169. The tangent is 5x + 12y = 169.

Answer

5x + 12y = 169. Radius slope 12/5, tangent slope −5/12, product −1 ✓.

h.en: Practice 11. Find the normal to x² + y² = 25 at (−4, 3).

body.en:
Working

The normal joins the centre (0, 0) to (−4, 3): slope 3/(−4) = −3/4, so y = −(3/4)x, that is 3x + 4y = 0.

Check

The point satisfies −12 + 12 = 0 ✓, and this line is perpendicular to the tangent −4x + 3y = 25 ✓.

h.en: Practice 12. Find k if the line 3x + 4y + k = 0 is tangent to x² + y² = 25.

body.en:
Working

  1. Distance from centre = |k|/5
  2. Set it equal to the radius: |k|/5 = 5
  3. k = ±25

Answer

k = ±25. Two tangents, 3x + 4y = ±25. Check: |25|/5 = 5 = r ✓.

h.en: Practice 13. Find the length of the tangent from (7, 1) to x² + y² − 4x + 2y − 4 = 0.

body.en:
Working

  1. Value at the point: 49 + 1 − 28 + 2 − 4 = 20
  2. Length = √20 = 2√5 ≈ 4.47

Answer

2√5 ≈ 4.47 units. The circle has centre (2, −1) and radius 3, and the point is √((7−2)² + (1+1)²) = √29 ≈ 5.39 from the centre, so a tangent of about 4.47 is consistent with √(29 − 9) ✓.

h.en: Practice 14. A circle passes through (2, 3) and has centre (2, 0). Find its equation and the tangent at (2, 3).

body.en:
Working

  1. r = 3, so (x − 2)² + y² = 9
  2. At (2, 3) the radius is vertical, so the tangent is horizontal: y = 3

Answer

(x − 2)² + y² = 9 and the tangent y = 3. The tangent is perpendicular to a vertical radius, which is exactly what the horizontal line gives.

h.en: Practice 15. Find the equation of the line through the point of intersection of x + y = 4 and x − y = 2 that is parallel to 3x + 2y = 5.

body.en:
Working

  1. Solving the pair: x = 3, y = 1
  2. Slope of 3x + 2y = 5 is −3/2
  3. y − 1 = −(3/2)(x − 3)
  4. 3x + 2y − 11 = 0

Check

The point (3, 1) satisfies 9 + 2 − 11 = 0 ✓ and the slope is −3/2 ✓.

title.en: Four forms of a straight line

terms.en: Rise over run; vertical lines have no finite slope.
The workhorse when one point and the slope are known.
Same statement as the slope formula, rearranged.
Only when both intercepts are non-zero.
Every line can be written this way.
Different constants; the same constants would mean one line.
In general form the test needs no division.
The modulus gives the acute angle.

items.f: xx₁ + yy₁ = a²  for  x² + y² = a²

terms.en: For other circles use the perpendicular-to-radius slope.
Two tangents, one on each side.
Less than r: secant. Greater than r: no contact.

q.en: Find the slope of the line joining (2, 3) and (6, 11).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Two points on the line.

Formula

m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)

Step-by-step solution

  1. Rise = 11 − 3 = 8
  2. Run = 6 − 2 = 4
  3. m = 8/4 = 2

Interpretation and check

m = 2. The line rises 2 units for every 1 to the right, so the angle with the x-axis is tan⁻¹2 ≈ 63.4° - consistent with a fairly steep line.

q.en: Find the equation of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Two points, so use the two-point form.

Formula

(y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁)

Step-by-step solution

  1. Slope = (8 − 2)/(3 − 1) = 3
  2. y − 2 = 3(x − 1)
  3. y = 3x − 1, that is 3x − y − 1 = 0

Interpretation and check

3x − y − 1 = 0. Check both points: 3 − 2 − 1 = 0 ✓ and 9 − 8 − 1 = 0 ✓. Always substitute both points - one is enough to catch most sign errors.

q.en: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line joining (0, 0) and (3, 4).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

First the slope of the given line, then the negative reciprocal.

Formula

m₁m₂ = −1

Step-by-step solution

  1. m₁ = 4/3
  2. m₂ = −3/4

Interpretation and check

−3/4. Check the product: (4/3)(−3/4) = −1 ✓. The perpendicular to a rising line must fall, so a negative slope is expected.

q.en: Find the equation of the line through (−2, 3) with slope 1/2.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

One point and the slope - point-slope form.

Formula

y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

Step-by-step solution

  1. y − 3 = ½(x + 2)
  2. 2y − 6 = x + 2
  3. x − 2y + 8 = 0

Interpretation and check

x − 2y + 8 = 0. Check the point: −2 − 6 + 8 = 0 ✓, and the slope −a/b = −1/(−2) = ½ ✓.

q.en: Find the equation of the line with x-intercept 3 and y-intercept −4.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Both intercepts are given, so use the intercept form.

Formula

x/a + y/b = 1

Step-by-step solution

  1. x/3 + y/(−4) = 1
  2. Multiply by 12: 4x − 3y = 12

Interpretation and check

4x − 3y = 12. Check both intercepts: at y = 0, x = 3 ✓; at x = 0, y = −4 ✓. The line crosses the y-axis below the origin, which the negative intercept records.

q.en: Reduce 3x + 4y − 12 = 0 to slope-intercept and intercept forms.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Solve for y for the first, and divide by 12 for the second.

Formula

slope = −a/b; intercepts = −c/a and −c/b

Step-by-step solution

  1. y = −(3/4)x + 3
  2. x/4 + y/3 = 1

Interpretation and check

Slope −3/4, y-intercept 3, x-intercept 4. Check: 3(4) + 0 − 12 = 0 ✓ and 0 + 4(3) − 12 = 0 ✓.

q.en: Find the line through (2, −3) parallel to 3x − 4y + 5 = 0.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Parallel lines differ only in the constant term.

Formula

family 3x − 4y + k = 0, then substitute the point

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3(2) − 4(−3) + k = 0
  2. 6 + 12 + k = 0 → k = −18
  3. 3x − 4y − 18 = 0

Interpretation and check

3x − 4y − 18 = 0. Check the point: 6 + 12 − 18 = 0 ✓, and the slope 3/4 matches the original line's 3/4 ✓.

q.en: Find the line through (1, 2) perpendicular to 2x + 3y = 6.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Swap the coefficients and change one sign, then fit the point.

Formula

perpendicular family 3x − 2y + k = 0

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3(1) − 2(2) + k = 0
  2. k = 1
  3. 3x − 2y + 1 = 0

Interpretation and check

3x − 2y + 1 = 0. Check perpendicularity from the general forms: a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 2(3) + 3(−2) = 0 ✓, and the point satisfies the equation ✓.

q.en: Find the acute angle between y = 2x + 1 and y = −x + 3.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Slopes m₁ = 2 and m₂ = −1.

Formula

tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)|

Step-by-step solution

  1. Numerator: |2 − (−1)| = 3
  2. Denominator: |1 + (2)(−1)| = 1
  3. tan θ = 3, θ = 71.57°

Interpretation and check

θ ≈ 71.6°. The lines are nowhere near parallel (slopes 2 and −1) and not perpendicular (product −2 ≠ −1), so a large acute angle is expected.

q.en: Find the angle between 3x − y + 4 = 0 and x + 2y − 5 = 0.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Convert both to slope form first.

Formula

tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)|

Step-by-step solution

  1. m₁ = 3 and m₂ = −1/2
  2. Numerator: |3 + 0.5| = 3.5, denominator: |1 − 1.5| = 0.5
  3. tan θ = 7, θ = 81.87°

Interpretation and check

θ ≈ 81.9°. Nearly perpendicular: a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 3(1) + (−1)(2) = 1, which is close to zero - so the angle must be close to 90° ✓.

q.en: Show that 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = 11 are parallel.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Compare the coefficient ratios.

Formula

parallel when a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2/4 = 3/6 = 1/2
  2. 5/11 ≠ 1/2
  3. The slopes are equal and the constants are not

Interpretation and check

Parallel. Both have slope −2/3. Because 5/11 ≠ 1/2, the lines are distinct - if the ratios had matched they would be the same line.

q.en: Show that 3x + 4y = 7 and 4x − 3y = 2 are perpendicular.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Use the general-form test, which avoids fractions.

Formula

a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 0

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3(4) + 4(−3)
  2. = 12 − 12 = 0

Interpretation and check

Perpendicular. Slope check: m₁ = −3/4 and m₂ = 4/3, product −1 ✓. The coefficient test is faster and has no sign traps.

q.en: Find the equation of the circle with centre (2, −3) and radius 5.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Centre-radius form, then expand if the general form is wanted.

Formula

(x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²

Step-by-step solution

  1. (x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 25
  2. x² − 4x + 4 + y² + 6y + 9 = 25
  3. x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0

Interpretation and check

(x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 25. Check a point: (7, −3) is 5 units right of the centre and satisfies 25 = 25 ✓. In the expanded form, −g = 2 and −f = −3 restore the centre.

q.en: Find the centre and radius of x² + y² − 6x + 8y − 11 = 0.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Compare with x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0.

Formula

centre (−g, −f), radius √(g² + f² − c)

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2g = −6 → g = −3; 2f = 8 → f = 4; c = −11
  2. Centre = (3, −4)
  3. r = √(9 + 16 + 11) = √36 = 6

Interpretation and check

Centre (3, −4), radius 6. Check by completing the square: (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 9 + 16 + 11 = 36 ✓.

q.en: Find the circle with (1, 2) and (5, 8) as ends of a diameter.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

The midpoint is the centre and half the distance is the radius.

Formula

centre = midpoint, r = ½√((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²)

Step-by-step solution

  1. Centre = (3, 5)
  2. Diameter = √(16 + 36) = √52 = 2√13, so r = √13
  3. (x − 3)² + (y − 5)² = 13

Interpretation and check

(x − 3)² + (y − 5)² = 13. Check both diameter ends: (1 − 3)² + (2 − 5)² = 4 + 9 = 13 ✓ and (5 − 3)² + (8 − 5)² = 4 + 9 = 13 ✓.

q.en: Find k so that (2, 3) lies on x² + y² + kx − 4y − 6 = 0.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

A point on the circle must satisfy its equation.

Formula

Substitute x = 2, y = 3

Step-by-step solution

  1. 4 + 9 + 2k − 12 − 6 = 0
  2. 2k − 5 = 0
  3. k = 5/2

Interpretation and check

k = 2.5. Check: 4 + 9 + 5 − 12 − 6 = 0 ✓. Substituting the point is the whole test - no geometry needed.

q.en: Find the tangent to x² + y² = 25 at (3, 4).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

The point lies on the circle because 9 + 16 = 25.

Formula

tangent at (x₁, y₁) to x² + y² = a² is xx₁ + yy₁ = a²

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3x + 4y = 25

Interpretation and check

3x + 4y = 25. Check the slopes: radius slope 4/3, tangent slope −3/4, product −1 ✓. The point (3, 4) satisfies the tangent equation ✓.

q.en: Find the tangent to x² + y² = 13 at (2, 3).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Check the point first: 4 + 9 = 13 ✓.

Formula

xx₁ + yy₁ = a²

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2x + 3y = 13

Interpretation and check

2x + 3y = 13. The radius slope is 3/2 and the tangent slope is −2/3; their product is −1 ✓.

q.en: Find the tangents to x² + y² = 25 that have slope 3/4.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Use the slope form of the tangent.

Formula

y = mx ± a√(1 + m²)

Step-by-step solution

  1. m = 3/4 and a = 5
  2. √(1 + 9/16) = 5/4
  3. c = ±5 × 5/4 = ±25/4
  4. y = (3/4)x ± 25/4, that is 3x − 4y ± 25 = 0

Interpretation and check

3x − 4y + 25 = 0 and 3x − 4y − 25 = 0. Check the distance from the centre: |25|/√(9 + 16) = 5 = radius ✓, so both lines just touch the circle.

q.en: Find the normal to x² + y² = 25 at (3, 4).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

The normal passes through the centre (0, 0).

Formula

the line through the centre and the point of contact

Step-by-step solution

  1. Slope = (4 − 0)/(3 − 0) = 4/3
  2. y = (4/3)x, that is 4x − 3y = 0

Interpretation and check

4x − 3y = 0. Check the point: 12 − 12 = 0 ✓, and the normal is perpendicular to the tangent 3x + 4y = 25 since (4/3)(−3/4) = −1 ✓.

q.en: Find the length of the tangent from (5, 1) to x² + y² = 25.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Use the power of the point.

Formula

length = √(x₁² + y₁² − a²)

Step-by-step solution

  1. = √(25 + 1 − 25)
  2. = √1
  3. = 1

Interpretation and check

1 unit. The point is just outside the circle (distance from centre √26 ≈ 5.099 > 5), so a short tangent is expected ✓.

q.en: Find the distance from (2, 3) to the line 3x + 4y − 5 = 0.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

The line is already in general form.

Formula

d = |ax₁ + by₁ + c|/√(a² + b²)

Step-by-step solution

  1. Numerator: |6 + 12 − 5| = 13
  2. Denominator: √25 = 5
  3. d = 13/5 = 2.6

Interpretation and check

2.6 units. The distance is positive by construction. Note that (2, 3) is far from the origin, so a distance of a few units from this line is plausible.

q.en: Find the distance between 3x + 4y = 5 and 3x + 4y = 15.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Parallel lines with the same coefficients.

Formula

d = |c₁ − c₂|/√(a² + b²)

Step-by-step solution

  1. |5 − 15| = 10
  2. √(9 + 16) = 5
  3. d = 10/5 = 2

Interpretation and check

2 units. Check with a point: (1.667, 0) lies on the first line and its distance from the second is |5 − 15|/5 = 2 ✓.

q.en: Find the line through (2, 3) parallel to the line joining (1, 1) and (4, 5).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

First find the slope of the joining line.

Formula

m = (5 − 1)/(4 − 1) = 4/3, then use point-slope

Step-by-step solution

  1. y − 3 = (4/3)(x − 2)
  2. 3y − 9 = 4x − 8
  3. 4x − 3y + 1 = 0

Interpretation and check

4x − 3y + 1 = 0. Check the point: 8 − 9 + 1 = 0 ✓ and the slope 4/3 matches ✓.

q.en: Find the circle through (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Because it passes through the origin, c = 0 in the general form.

Formula

x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0

Step-by-step solution

  1. Through (0, 0): c = 0
  2. Through (4, 0): 16 + 8g = 0 → g = −2
  3. Through (0, 3): 9 + 6f = 0 → f = −3/2
  4. x² + y² − 4x − 3y = 0

Interpretation and check

x² + y² − 4x − 3y = 0. Centre (2, 1.5) and radius √(4 + 2.25) = 2.5 - exactly half the hypotenuse of the 3-4-5 triangle, as a circle through the three vertices of a right triangle must be.

q.en: Find c so that y = 2x + c is a tangent to x² + y² = 25.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Tangency means the distance from the centre equals the radius.

Formula

distance from (0, 0) to 2x − y + c = 0 equals 5

Step-by-step solution

  1. |c|/√(4 + 1) = 5
  2. |c| = 5√5
  3. c = ±5√5 ≈ ±11.18

Interpretation and check

c = ±5√5. Two parallel tangents, one on each side of the circle. Check: the distance from the origin to 2x − y + 5√5 = 0 is 5√5/√5 = 5 = r ✓.

q.en: Define the slope of a line.

a.en: m = tan θ, the tangent of the angle with the positive x-axis; also (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁).

q.en: Write the two-point form.

a.en: (y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁).

q.en: What is the slope of a vertical line?

a.en: It is not defined; the equation is x = a.

q.en: Write the intercept form of a line.

a.en: x/a + y/b = 1, where a and b are the x- and y-intercepts.

q.en: How do you find the slope from ax + by + c = 0?

a.en: m = −a/b.

q.en: Give the condition for two lines to be parallel.

a.en: m₁ = m₂, or a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ in general form.

q.en: Give the condition for two lines to be perpendicular.

a.en: m₁m₂ = −1, or a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 0.

q.en: State the angle-between-lines formula.

a.en: tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)|.

q.en: What does the formula give when 1 + m₁m₂ = 0?

a.en: The denominator vanishes, so θ = 90° - the lines are perpendicular.

q.en: Write the distance from a point to a line.

a.en: d = |ax₁ + by₁ + c|/√(a² + b²).

q.en: How do you find the distance between two parallel lines?

a.en: Write both in the same form and use |c₁ − c₂|/√(a² + b²).

q.en: Write the equation of a circle with centre (h, k) and radius r.

a.en: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r².

q.en: What are the centre and radius of x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0?

a.en: Centre (−g, −f), radius √(g² + f² − c).

q.en: How do you find the centre when the ends of a diameter are given?

a.en: The midpoint of the two ends; the radius is half the distance between them.

q.en: What is the tangent at (x₁, y₁) to x² + y² = a²?

a.en: xx₁ + yy₁ = a².

q.en: Why is the tangent perpendicular to the radius?

a.en: The radius to the point of contact is the shortest distance to the tangent, so the two are perpendicular.

q.en: Write the normal to a circle at a point.

a.en: The line joining the centre to that point, because every normal passes through the centre.

q.en: How do you test whether a line is tangent to a circle?

a.en: The perpendicular distance from the centre equals the radius.

q.en: Give the tangents of slope m to x² + y² = a².

a.en: y = mx ± a√(1 + m²).

q.en: What is the length of the tangent from (x₁, y₁) to x² + y² = a²?

a.en: √(x₁² + y₁² − a²).
